text: ¶Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know intelligence;

title: Proverbs 4:2
text: for I give you good doctrine: forsake ye not my law.

title: Proverbs 4:3
text: For I was a son unto my father, tender and an only one in the sight of my mother.

title: Proverbs 4:4
text: And he taught me, and said unto me, Let thy heart retain my words; keep my commandments and live.

title: Proverbs 4:5
text: Get wisdom, get intelligence: forget [it] not; neither decline from the words of my mouth.

title: Proverbs 4:6
text: Forsake her not, and she shall keep thee; love her, and she shall preserve thee.

title: Proverbs 4:7
text: The beginning of wisdom [is], Get wisdom; and with all thy getting get intelligence.

title: Proverbs 4:8
text: Exalt her, and she shall promote thee; she shall bring thee to honour when thou dost embrace her.

title: Proverbs 4:9
text: She shall give to thy head a garland of grace; a crown of glory will she bestow upon thee.

title: Proverbs 4:10
text: Hear, my son, and receive my sayings, and the years of thy life shall be multiplied.

title: Proverbs 4:11
text: I will teach thee in the way of wisdom, I will lead thee in paths of uprightness.

title: Proverbs 4:12
text: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.

title: Proverbs 4:13
text: Take fast hold of instruction, let [her] not go: keep her, for she is thy life.

title: Proverbs 4:14
text: ¶Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil [men]:

title: Proverbs 4:15
text: avoid it, pass not by it; turn from it, and pass away.

title: Proverbs 4:16
text: For they sleep not except they have done mischief, and their sleep is taken away unless they have caused [some] to fall.

title: Proverbs 4:17
text: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.

title: Proverbs 4:18
text: But the path of the righteous is as the shining light, going on and brightening until the day be fully come.

title: Proverbs 4:19
text: The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.

title: Proverbs 4:20
text: ¶My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings.

title: Proverbs 4:21
text: Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thy heart.

title: Proverbs 4:22
text: For they are life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.

title: Proverbs 4:23
text: Keep thy heart more than anything that is guarded; for out of it are the issues of life.

title: Proverbs 4:24
text: Put away from thee perverseness of mouth, and corrupt lips put far from thee.

title: Proverbs 4:25
text: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee.

title: Proverbs 4:26
text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be well-ordered.

title: Proverbs 4:27
text: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left; remove thy foot from evil.

title: Proverbs 5:1
text: ¶My son, attend unto my wisdom, incline thine ear to my understanding;

title: Proverbs 5:2
text: that thou mayest keep reflection, and that thy lips may preserve knowledge.

title: Proverbs 5:3
text: For the lips of the strange woman drop honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil;

title: Proverbs 5:4
text: but her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.

title: Proverbs 5:5
text: Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on Sheol.

title: Proverbs 5:6
text: Lest she should ponder the path of life, her ways wander, she knoweth not [whither].

title: Proverbs 5:7
text: And now, children, hearken unto me, and depart not from the words of my mouth.

title: Proverbs 5:8
text: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:

title: Proverbs 5:9
text: lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel;

title: Proverbs 5:10
text: lest strangers be filled with thy wealth, and the fruits of thy toil [come] into the house of a stranger;

title: Proverbs 5:11
text: and thou mourn in thine end, when thy flesh and thy body are consumed;

title: Proverbs 5:12
text: and thou say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof!

title: Proverbs 5:13
text: and I have not hearkened unto the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to those that instructed me;

title: Proverbs 5:14
text: I was well nigh in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly.

title: Proverbs 5:15
text: ¶Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.

title: Proverbs 5:16
text: Thy fountains shall be poured forth, as water-brooks in the broadways.

title: Proverbs 5:17
text: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers' with thee.

title: Proverbs 5:18
text: Let thy fountain be blessed; and have joy of the wife of thy youth.

title: Proverbs 5:19
text: As a lovely hind and a graceful roe, let her breasts satisfy thee at all times: be thou ravished continually with her love.

title: Proverbs 5:20
text: And why shouldest thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?

title: Proverbs 5:21
text: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Jehovah, and he pondereth all his paths.

title: Proverbs 5:22
text: His own iniquities shall take the wicked, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sin.

title: Proverbs 5:23
text: He shall die for want of discipline; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.

title: Proverbs 6:1
text: ¶My son, if thou hast become surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand for a stranger,

title: Proverbs 6:2
text: thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.

title: Proverbs 6:3
text: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, since thou hast come into the hand of thy friend: go, humble thyself, and be urgent with thy friend.

title: Proverbs 6:4
text: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids:

title: Proverbs 6:5
text: deliver thyself as a gazelle from the hand [of the hunter], and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.

title: Proverbs 6:6
text: ¶Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways and be wise:

title: Proverbs 6:7
text: which having no chief, overseer, or ruler,

title: Proverbs 6:8
text: provideth her bread in the summer, [and] gathereth her food in the harvest.

title: Proverbs 6:9
text: How long, sluggard, wilt thou lie down? When wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?

title: Proverbs 6:10
text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest!

title: Proverbs 6:11
text: So shall thy poverty come as a roving plunderer, and thy penury as an armed man.

title: Proverbs 6:12
text: ¶A man of Belial, a wicked person, is he that goeth about with a perverse mouth;

title: Proverbs 6:13
text: he winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet, he teacheth with his fingers;

title: Proverbs 6:14
text: deceits are in his heart; he deviseth mischief at all times, he soweth discords.

title: Proverbs 6:15
text: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly: in a moment shall he be broken, and without remedy.

title: Proverbs 6:16
text: These six [things] doth Jehovah hate, yea, seven are an abomination unto him:

title: Proverbs 6:17
text: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood;

title: Proverbs 6:18
text: a heart that deviseth wicked imaginations; feet that are swift in running to mischief;

title: Proverbs 6:19
text: a false witness that uttereth lies, and he that soweth discords among brethren.

title: Proverbs 6:20
text: ¶My son, observe thy father's commandment, and forsake not the teaching of thy mother;

title: Proverbs 6:21
text: bind them continually upon thy heart, tie them about thy neck:

title: Proverbs 6:22
text: when thou walkest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and [when] thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.

title: Proverbs 6:23
text: For the commandment is a lamp, and the teaching a light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:

title: Proverbs 6:24
text: to keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.

title: Proverbs 6:25
text: Lust not after her beauty in thy heart, neither let her take thee with her eyelids;

title: Proverbs 6:26
text: for by means of a whorish woman [a man is brought] to a loaf of bread, and another's wife doth hunt for the precious soul.

title: Proverbs 6:27
text: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his garments not be burned?

title: Proverbs 6:28
text: Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?

title: Proverbs 6:29
text: So he that goeth in to his neighbour's wife: whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.

title: Proverbs 6:30
text: They do not despise a thief, if he steal to satisfy his soul when he is hungry:

title: Proverbs 6:31
text: and if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house.

title: Proverbs 6:32
text: Whoso committeth adultery with a woman is void of understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul.

title: Proverbs 6:33
text: A wound and contempt shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.

title: Proverbs 6:34
text: For jealousy is the rage of a man, and he will not spare in the day of vengeance;

title: Proverbs 6:35
text: he will not regard any ransom, neither will he rest content though thou multipliest [thy] gifts.

title: Proverbs 7:1
text: ¶My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee.

title: Proverbs 7:2
text: Keep my commandments, and live; and my teaching, as the apple of thine eye.

title: Proverbs 7:3
text: Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the tablet of thy heart.

title: Proverbs 7:4
text: Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister, and call intelligence [thy] kinswoman:

title: Proverbs 7:5
text: that they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger who flattereth with her words.

title: Proverbs 7:6
text: ¶For at the window of my house, I looked forth through my lattice,

title: Proverbs 7:7
text: and I beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the sons, a young man void of understanding,

title: Proverbs 7:8
text: passing through the street near her corner; and he went the way to her house,

title: Proverbs 7:9
text: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, in the blackness of night and the darkness.

title: Proverbs 7:10
text: And behold, there met him a woman in the attire of a harlot, and subtle of heart.

title: Proverbs 7:11
text: She is clamorous and unmanageable; her feet abide not in her house:

title: Proverbs 7:12
text: now without, now in the broadways, --and she lieth in wait at every corner.

title: Proverbs 7:13
text: And she caught him and kissed him, and with an impudent face said unto him,

title: Proverbs 7:14
text: I have peace-offerings with me; this day have I paid my vows:

title: Proverbs 7:15
text: therefore came I forth to meet thee, to seek earnestly thy face, and I have found thee.

title: Proverbs 7:16
text: I have decked my bed with tapestry coverlets of variegated linen from Egypt;

title: Proverbs 7:17
text: I have perfumed my couch with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

title: Proverbs 7:18
text: Come, let us revel in love until the morning, let us delight ourselves with loves.

title: Proverbs 7:19
text: For the husband is not at home, he is gone a long journey;

title: Proverbs 7:20
text: he hath taken the money-bag with him, he will come home on the day of the full moon.

title: Proverbs 7:21
text: With her much enticement she beguiled him; with the smoothness of her lips she constrained him.

title: Proverbs 7:22
text: He went after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, and as stocks [serve] for the correction of the fool;

title: Proverbs 7:23
text: till an arrow strike through his liver: as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for its life.

title: Proverbs 7:24
text: ¶And now, ye sons, hearken unto me, and attend to the words of my mouth.

title: Proverbs 7:25
text: Let not thy heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths:

title: Proverbs 7:26
text: for she hath cast down many wounded, and all slain by her were strong.

title: Proverbs 7:27
text: Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the chambers of death.

title: Proverbs 8:1
text: ¶Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding give forth her voice?

title: Proverbs 8:2
text: On the top of high places by the way, at the cross-paths she taketh her stand.

title: Proverbs 8:3
text: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud.

title: Proverbs 8:4
text: Unto you, men, I call, and my voice is to the sons of man:

title: Proverbs 8:5
text: O ye simple, understand prudence; and ye foolish, understand sense.

title: Proverbs 8:6
text: Hear, for I will speak excellent things, and the opening of my lips shall be right things.

title: Proverbs 8:7
text: For my palate shall meditate truth, and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.

title: Proverbs 8:8
text: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing tortuous or perverse in them.

title: Proverbs 8:9
text: They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.

title: Proverbs 8:10
text: Receive my instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than choice gold:

title: Proverbs 8:11
text: for wisdom is better than rubies, and all the things that may be desired are not equal to it.

title: Proverbs 8:12
text: ¶I wisdom dwell [with] prudence, and find the knowledge [which cometh] of reflection.

title: Proverbs 8:13
text: The fear of Jehovah is to hate evil; pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth do I hate.

title: Proverbs 8:14
text: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am intelligence; I have strength.

title: Proverbs 8:15
text: By me kings reign, and rulers make just decrees;

title: Proverbs 8:16
text: by me princes rule, and nobles, all the judges of the earth.

title: Proverbs 8:17
text: I love those that love me; and they that seek me early shall find me.

title: Proverbs 8:18
text: Riches and honour are with me; durable wealth and righteousness.

title: Proverbs 8:19
text: My fruit is better than fine gold, yea, than pure gold; and my revenue than choice silver.

title: Proverbs 8:20
text: I walk in the path of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of judgment:

title: Proverbs 8:21
text: that I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasuries.

title: Proverbs 8:22
text: ¶Jehovah possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.

title: Proverbs 8:23
text: I was set up from eternity, from the beginning, before the earth was.

title: Proverbs 8:24
text: When there were no depths, I was brought forth, when there were no fountains abounding with water.

title: Proverbs 8:25
text: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth;

title: Proverbs 8:26
text: while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.

title: Proverbs 8:27
text: When he prepared the heavens I was there; when he ordained the circle upon the face of the deep;

title: Proverbs 8:28
text: when he established the skies above, when the fountains of the deep became strong;

title: Proverbs 8:29
text: when he imposed on the sea his decree that the waters should not pass his commandment, when he appointed the foundations of the earth:

title: Proverbs 8:30
text: then I was by him [his] nursling, and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;

title: Proverbs 8:31
text: rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth, and my delights [were] with the sons of men.

title: Proverbs 8:32
text: ¶And now, sons, hearken unto me, and blessed are they that keep my ways:

title: Proverbs 8:33
text: hear instruction and be wise, and refuse it not.

title: Proverbs 8:34
text: Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.

title: Proverbs 8:35
text: For whoso findeth me findeth life, and obtaineth favour of Jehovah;

title: Proverbs 8:36
text: but he that sinneth against me doeth violence to his own soul: all they that hate me love death.

title: Proverbs 9:1
text: ¶Wisdom hath built her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars;

title: Proverbs 9:2
text: she hath slaughtered her cattle, she hath mingled her wine, she hath also prepared her table;

title: Proverbs 9:3
text: she hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the summits of the high places of the city,

title: Proverbs 9:4
text: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither. To him that is void of understanding, she saith,

title: Proverbs 9:5
text: Come, eat ye of my bread, and drink of the wine that I have mingled.

title: Proverbs 9:6
text: Forsake follies and live, and go in the way of intelligence.

title: Proverbs 9:7
text: He that instructeth a scorner getteth to himself shame; and he that reproveth a wicked [man] [getteth] to himself a blot.

title: Proverbs 9:8
text: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee; reprove a wise [man], and he will love thee.

title: Proverbs 9:9
text: Impart to a wise [man], and he will become yet wiser; teach a righteous [man], and he will increase learning.

title: Proverbs 9:10
text: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom; and the knowledge of the Holy is intelligence.

title: Proverbs 9:11
text: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and years of life shall be added to thee.

title: Proverbs 9:12
text: If thou art wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself; and if thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it.

title: Proverbs 9:13
text: ¶The foolish woman is clamorous; she is stupid, and knoweth nothing.

title: Proverbs 9:14
text: And she sitteth at the entry of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

title: Proverbs 9:15
text: to call passers-by who go right on their ways:

title: Proverbs 9:16
text: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither. And to him that is void of understanding she saith,

title: Proverbs 9:17
text: Stolen waters are sweet, and the bread of secrecy is pleasant.

title: Proverbs 9:18
text: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; [that] her guests are in the depths of Sheol.

title: Proverbs 10:1
text: ¶The Proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father; but a foolish son is the grief of his mother.

title: Proverbs 10:2
text: ¶Treasures of wickedness profit nothing; but righteousness delivereth from death.

title: Proverbs 10:3
text: Jehovah suffereth not the soul of the righteous [man] to famish; but he repelleth the craving of the wicked.

title: Proverbs 10:4
text: ¶He cometh to want that dealeth with a slack hand; but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.

title: Proverbs 10:5
text: ¶He that gathereth in summer is a wise son; he that sleepeth in harvest is a son that causeth shame.

title: Proverbs 10:6
text: ¶Blessings are upon the head of a righteous [man]; but the mouth of the wicked covereth violence.

title: Proverbs 10:7
text: ¶The memory of the righteous [man] shall be blessed; but the name of the wicked shall rot.

title: Proverbs 10:8
text: ¶The wise in heart receiveth commandments; but a prating fool shall fall.

title: Proverbs 10:9
text: ¶He that walketh in integrity walketh securely; but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.

title: Proverbs 10:10
text: ¶He that winketh with the eye causeth grief, and a prating fool shall fall.

title: Proverbs 10:11
text: ¶The mouth of a righteous [man] is a fountain of life; but the mouth of the wicked covereth violence.

title: Proverbs 10:12
text: ¶Hatred stirreth up strifes; but love covereth all transgressions.

title: Proverbs 10:13
text: ¶In the lips of an intelligent [man] wisdom is found; but a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding.

title: Proverbs 10:14
text: ¶The wise lay up knowledge; but the mouth of the fool is near destruction.

title: Proverbs 10:15
text: ¶The rich man's wealth is his strong city; the destruction of the poor is their poverty.

title: Proverbs 10:16
text: ¶The labour of a righteous [man] [tendeth] to life; the revenue of a wicked [man], to sin.

title: Proverbs 10:17
text: ¶Keeping instruction is the path to life; but he that forsaketh reproof goeth astray.

title: Proverbs 10:18
text: ¶He that covereth hatred hath lying lips, and he that sendeth forth a slander is a fool.

title: Proverbs 10:19
text: ¶In the multitude of words there wanteth not transgression; but he that restraineth his lips doeth wisely.

title: Proverbs 10:20
text: ¶The tongue of the righteous [man] is [as] choice silver; the heart of the wicked is little worth.

title: Proverbs 10:21
text: The lips of a righteous [man] feed many; but fools die for want of understanding.

title: Proverbs 10:22
text: ¶The blessing of Jehovah, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow to it.

title: Proverbs 10:23
text: ¶It is as sport to a foolish [man] to do wickedness; but a man of understanding hath wisdom.

title: Proverbs 10:24
text: ¶The fear of a wicked [man], it shall come upon him; but the desire of the righteous shall be granted.

title: Proverbs 10:25
text: As a whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no [more]; but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.

title: Proverbs 10:26
text: ¶As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to them that send him.

title: Proverbs 10:27
text: ¶The fear of Jehovah prolongeth days; but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.

title: Proverbs 10:28
text: The hope of the righteous is joy; but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.

title: Proverbs 10:29
text: ¶The way of Jehovah is strength to the perfect [man], but destruction to the workers of iniquity.

title: Proverbs 10:30
text: The righteous [man] shall never be moved; but the wicked shall not inhabit the land.

title: Proverbs 10:31
text: ¶The mouth of a righteous [man] putteth forth wisdom; but the froward tongue shall be cut out.

title: Proverbs 10:32
text: The lips of a righteous [man] know what is acceptable; but the mouth of the wicked is frowardness.

title: Proverbs 11:1
text: ¶A false balance is an abomination to Jehovah; but a just weight is his delight.

title: Proverbs 11:2
text: ¶[When] pride cometh, then cometh shame; but with the lowly is wisdom.

title: Proverbs 11:3
text: ¶The integrity of the upright guideth them; but the crookedness of the unfaithful destroyeth them.

title: Proverbs 11:4
text: ¶Wealth profiteth not in the day of wrath; but righteousness delivereth from death.

title: Proverbs 11:5
text: ¶The righteousness of the perfect maketh plain his way; but the wicked falleth by his own wickedness.

title: Proverbs 11:6
text: The righteousness of the upright delivereth them; but the treacherous are taken in their own craving.

title: Proverbs 11:7
text: ¶When a wicked man dieth, [his] expectation shall perish; and the hope of evil [men] perisheth.

title: Proverbs 11:8
text: ¶The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.

title: Proverbs 11:9
text: ¶With his mouth a hypocrite destroyeth his neighbour; but through knowledge are the righteous delivered.

title: Proverbs 11:10
text: ¶When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth; and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.

title: Proverbs 11:11
text: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted; but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.

title: Proverbs 11:12
text: ¶He that despiseth his neighbour is void of heart; but a man of understanding holdeth his peace.

title: Proverbs 11:13
text: He that goeth about talebearing revealeth secrets; but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

title: Proverbs 11:14
text: ¶Where no advice is, the people fall; but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

title: Proverbs 11:15
text: ¶It goeth ill with him that is surety for another; but he that hateth suretyship is secure.

title: Proverbs 11:16
text: ¶A gracious woman retaineth honour; and the violent retain riches.

title: Proverbs 11:17
text: ¶The merciful man doeth good to his own soul; but the cruel troubleth his own flesh.

title: Proverbs 11:18
text: ¶The wicked worketh a deceitful work; but he that soweth righteousness hath a sure reward.

title: Proverbs 11:19
text: ¶As righteousness [tendeth] to life, so he that pursueth evil [doeth it] to his own death.

title: Proverbs 11:20
text: ¶The perverse in heart are abomination to Jehovah; but they that are perfect in [their] way are his delight.

title: Proverbs 11:21
text: ¶Hand for hand! an evil [man] shall not be held innocent; but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

title: Proverbs 11:22
text: ¶A fair woman who is without discretion, is [as] a gold ring in a swine's snout.

title: Proverbs 11:23
text: ¶The desire of the righteous is only good; the expectation of the wicked is wrath.

title: Proverbs 11:24
text: ¶There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is right, but [it tendeth] only to want.

title: Proverbs 11:25
text: ¶The liberal soul shall be made fat, and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

title: Proverbs 11:26
text: ¶He that withholdeth corn, the people curse him; but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.

title: Proverbs 11:27
text: ¶He that is earnest after good seeketh favour; but he that searcheth for mischief, it shall come upon him.

title: Proverbs 11:28
text: ¶He that trusteth in his riches shall fall; but the righteous shall flourish as a leaf.

title: Proverbs 11:29
text: ¶He that troubleth his own house shall inherit wind; and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.

title: Proverbs 11:30
text: ¶The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and the wise winneth souls.

title: Proverbs 11:31
text: ¶Behold, the righteous shall be requited on the earth: how much more the wicked and the sinner.

title: Proverbs 12:1
text: ¶Whoso loveth discipline loveth knowledge, but he that hateth reproof is brutish.

title: Proverbs 12:2
text: ¶A good [man] obtaineth favour of Jehovah; but a man of mischievous devices will he condemn.

title: Proverbs 12:3
text: ¶A man shall not be established by wickedness; but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

title: Proverbs 12:4
text: ¶A woman of worth is a crown to her husband; but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.

title: Proverbs 12:5
text: ¶The thoughts of the righteous are right; the counsels of the wicked are deceit.

title: Proverbs 12:6
text: ¶The words of the wicked are a lying-in-wait for blood; but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.

title: Proverbs 12:7
text: ¶Overthrow the wicked, and they are no [more]; but the house of the righteous shall stand.

title: Proverbs 12:8
text: ¶A man is commended according to his wisdom; but he that is of a perverted heart shall be despised.

title: Proverbs 12:9
text: ¶Better is he that is lightly esteemed, and hath a servant, than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.

title: Proverbs 12:10
text: ¶A righteous man is concerned for the life of his beast; but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.

title: Proverbs 12:11
text: ¶He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread; but he that followeth the worthless is void of understanding.

title: Proverbs 12:12
text: ¶The wicked desireth the net of evil [men]; but the root of the righteous yieldeth [fruit].

title: Proverbs 12:13
text: ¶In the transgression of the lips is an evil snare; but a righteous [man] shall go forth out of trouble.

title: Proverbs 12:14
text: ¶A man is satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth; and the recompense of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him.

title: Proverbs 12:15
text: ¶The way of a fool is right in his own eyes; but he that is wise hearkeneth unto counsel.

title: Proverbs 12:16
text: ¶The vexation of the fool is presently known; but a prudent [man] covereth shame.

title: Proverbs 12:17
text: ¶He that uttereth truth sheweth forth righteousness; but a false witness deceit.

title: Proverbs 12:18
text: ¶There is that babbleth like the piercings of a sword; but the tongue of the wise is health.

title: Proverbs 12:19
text: ¶The lip of truth shall be established for ever; but a lying tongue is but for a moment.

title: Proverbs 12:20
text: ¶Deceit is in the heart of them that devise evil; but to the counsellors of peace is joy.

title: Proverbs 12:21
text: ¶There shall no evil happen to a righteous [man]; but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.

title: Proverbs 12:22
text: ¶Lying lips are an abomination to Jehovah; but they that deal truly are his delight.

title: Proverbs 12:23
text: ¶A prudent man concealeth knowledge; but the heart of the foolish proclaimeth folly.

title: Proverbs 12:24
text: ¶The hand of the diligent shall bear rule; but the slothful [hand] shall be under tribute.

title: Proverbs 12:25
text: ¶Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop; but a good word maketh it glad.

title: Proverbs 12:26
text: ¶The righteous guideth his neighbour; but the way of the wicked misleadeth them.

title: Proverbs 12:27
text: ¶The slothful roasteth not what he took in hunting; but man's precious substance is to the diligent.

title: Proverbs 12:28
text: ¶In the path of righteousness is life, and in the pathway thereof there is no death.

title: Proverbs 13:1
text: ¶A wise son [heareth] his father's instruction; but a scorner heareth not rebuke.

title: Proverbs 13:2
text: ¶A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth; but the soul of the treacherous, violence.

title: Proverbs 13:3
text: ¶He that guardeth his mouth keepeth his soul; destruction shall be to him that openeth wide his lips.

title: Proverbs 13:4
text: ¶A sluggard's soul desireth and hath nothing; but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.

title: Proverbs 13:5
text: ¶A righteous [man] hateth lying; but the wicked maketh himself odious and cometh to shame.

title: Proverbs 13:6
text: ¶Righteousness preserveth him that is perfect in the way; but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.

title: Proverbs 13:7
text: ¶There is that feigneth himself rich, and hath nothing; there is that maketh himself poor, and hath great wealth.

title: Proverbs 13:8
text: ¶The ransom of a man's life is his riches; but the indigent heareth not rebuke.

title: Proverbs 13:9
text: ¶The light of the righteous rejoiceth; but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

title: Proverbs 13:10
text: ¶By pride there only cometh contention; but with the well-advised is wisdom.

title: Proverbs 13:11
text: ¶Wealth [gotten] by vanity diminisheth; but he that gathereth by manual-labour shall increase [it].

title: Proverbs 13:12
text: ¶Hope deferred maketh the heart sick; but the desire [that] cometh to pass is a tree of life.

title: Proverbs 13:13
text: ¶Whoso despiseth the word shall be held by it; but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.

title: Proverbs 13:14
text: ¶The teaching of the wise [man] is a fountain of life, to turn away from the snares of death.

title: Proverbs 13:15
text: ¶Good understanding procureth favour; but the way of the treacherous is hard.

title: Proverbs 13:16
text: ¶Every prudent [man] acteth with knowledge; but the foolish layeth open [his] folly.

title: Proverbs 13:17
text: ¶A wicked messenger falleth into evil; but a faithful ambassador is health.

title: Proverbs 13:18
text: ¶Poverty and shame shall be [to] him that refuseth instruction; but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.

title: Proverbs 13:19
text: ¶The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul; but it is abomination to the foolish to depart from evil.

title: Proverbs 13:20
text: ¶He that walketh with wise [men] becometh wise; but a companion of the foolish will be depraved.

title: Proverbs 13:21
text: ¶Evil pursueth sinners; but to the righteous good shall be repaid.

title: Proverbs 13:22
text: ¶A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children; but the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the righteous [man].

title: Proverbs 13:23
text: ¶Much food is in the tillage of the poor; but there is that is lost for want of judgment.

title: Proverbs 13:24
text: ¶He that spareth his rod hateth his son; but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.

title: Proverbs 13:25
text: ¶The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul; but the belly of the wicked shall want.

title: Proverbs 14:1
text: ¶The wisdom of women buildeth their house; but folly plucketh it down with her hands.

title: Proverbs 14:2
text: ¶He that walketh in his uprightness feareth Jehovah; but he that is perverted in his ways despiseth him.

title: Proverbs 14:3
text: ¶In the fool's mouth is a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.

title: Proverbs 14:4
text: ¶Where no oxen are, the crib is clean; but much increase is by the strength of the ox.

title: Proverbs 14:5
text: ¶A faithful witness will not lie; but a false witness uttereth lies.

title: Proverbs 14:6
text: ¶A scorner seeketh wisdom, and there is none [for him]; but knowledge is easy unto the intelligent.

title: Proverbs 14:7
text: ¶Go from the presence of a foolish man, in whom thou perceivest not the lips of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 14:8
text: ¶The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way; but the folly of the foolish is deceit.

title: Proverbs 14:9
text: ¶Fools make a mock at trespass; but for the upright there is favour.

title: Proverbs 14:10
text: ¶The heart knoweth its own bitterness, and a stranger doth not intermeddle with its joy.

title: Proverbs 14:11
text: ¶The house of the wicked shall be overthrown; but the tent of the upright shall flourish.

title: Proverbs 14:12
text: ¶There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof is the ways of death.

title: Proverbs 14:13
text: ¶Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, and the end of mirth is sadness.

title: Proverbs 14:14
text: ¶The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways, and the good man from what is in himself.

title: Proverbs 14:15
text: ¶The simple believeth every word; but the prudent [man] heedeth his going.

title: Proverbs 14:16
text: ¶A wise [man] feareth and departeth from evil; but the foolish is overbearing and confident.

title: Proverbs 14:17
text: ¶He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly, and a man of mischievous devices is hated.

title: Proverbs 14:18
text: ¶The simple inherit folly; but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

title: Proverbs 14:19
text: ¶The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous [man].

title: Proverbs 14:20
text: ¶He that is poor is hated even of his own neighbour; but the rich hath many friends.

title: Proverbs 14:21
text: ¶He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth; but he that is gracious to the afflicted, happy is he.

title: Proverbs 14:22
text: ¶Do they not err that devise evil? but loving-kindness and truth are for those that devise good.

title: Proverbs 14:23
text: ¶In all labour there is profit; but the talk of the lips [tendeth] only to want.

title: Proverbs 14:24
text: ¶The crown of the wise is their riches; the folly of the foolish is folly.

title: Proverbs 14:25
text: ¶A true witness delivereth souls; but deceit uttereth lies.

title: Proverbs 14:26
text: ¶In the fear of Jehovah is strong confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.

title: Proverbs 14:27
text: The fear of Jehovah is a fountain of life, to turn away from the snares of death.

title: Proverbs 14:28
text: ¶In the multitude of people is the king's glory; but in the lack of people is the ruin of a prince.

title: Proverbs 14:29
text: ¶He that is slow to anger is of great understanding; but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

title: Proverbs 14:30
text: ¶A sound heart is the life of the flesh; but envy the rottenness of the bones.

title: Proverbs 14:31
text: ¶He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker; but he that honoureth Him is gracious to the needy.

title: Proverbs 14:32
text: ¶The wicked is driven away by his evil-doing; but the righteous trusteth, [even] in his death.

title: Proverbs 14:33
text: ¶Wisdom resteth in the heart of the intelligent [man]; but that which is in the foolish maketh itself known.

title: Proverbs 14:34
text: ¶Righteousness exalteth a nation; but sin is a reproach to peoples.

title: Proverbs 14:35
text: ¶The king's favour is toward a wise servant; but his wrath is [against] him that causeth shame.

title: Proverbs 15:1
text: ¶A soft answer turneth away fury; but a grievous word stirreth up anger.

title: Proverbs 15:2
text: ¶The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright; but the mouth of the foolish poureth out folly.

title: Proverbs 15:3
text: ¶The eyes of Jehovah are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

title: Proverbs 15:4
text: ¶Gentleness of tongue is a tree of life; but crookedness therein is a breaking of the spirit.

title: Proverbs 15:5
text: ¶A fool despiseth his father's instruction; but he that regardeth reproof becometh prudent.

title: Proverbs 15:6
text: ¶In the house of a righteous [man] is much treasure; but in the revenue of a wicked [man] is disturbance.

title: Proverbs 15:7
text: ¶The lips of the wise disperse knowledge, but not so the heart of the foolish.

title: Proverbs 15:8
text: ¶The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; but the prayer of the upright is his delight.

title: Proverbs 15:9
text: ¶The way of a wicked [man] is an abomination to Jehovah; but him that pursueth righteousness he loveth.

title: Proverbs 15:10
text: ¶Grievous correction is for him that forsaketh the path; he that hateth reproof shall die.

title: Proverbs 15:11
text: ¶Sheol and destruction are before Jehovah; how much more then the hearts of the children of men!

title: Proverbs 15:12
text: ¶A scorner loveth not one that reproveth him; he will not go unto the wise.

title: Proverbs 15:13
text: ¶A joyful heart maketh a cheerful countenance; but by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.

title: Proverbs 15:14
text: ¶The heart of an intelligent [man] seeketh knowledge; but the mouth of the foolish feedeth on folly.

title: Proverbs 15:15
text: ¶All the days of the afflicted are evil; but a cheerful heart is a continual feast.

title: Proverbs 15:16
text: ¶Better is little with the fear of Jehovah than great store and disquietude therewith.

title: Proverbs 15:17
text: Better is a meal of herbs where love is, than a fatted ox and hatred therewith.

title: Proverbs 15:18
text: ¶A furious man stirreth up contention; but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.

title: Proverbs 15:19
text: ¶The way of the sluggard is as a hedge of thorns; but the path of the upright is made plain.

title: Proverbs 15:20
text: ¶A wise son maketh a glad father; but a foolish man despiseth his mother.

title: Proverbs 15:21
text: ¶Folly is joy to him that is void of sense; but a man of understanding regulateth his walk.

title: Proverbs 15:22
text: ¶Without counsel purposes are disappointed; but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.

title: Proverbs 15:23
text: ¶A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth; and a word in its season, how good is it!

title: Proverbs 15:24
text: ¶The path of life is upwards for the wise, that he may depart from Sheol beneath.

title: Proverbs 15:25
text: ¶Jehovah plucketh up the house of the proud; but he establisheth the boundary of the widow.

title: Proverbs 15:26
text: ¶The thoughts of the evil [man] are an abomination to Jehovah; but pure words are pleasant.

title: Proverbs 15:27
text: ¶He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; but he that hateth gifts shall live.

title: Proverbs 15:28
text: ¶The heart of a righteous [man] studieth to answer; but the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.

title: Proverbs 15:29
text: ¶Jehovah is far from the wicked; but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.

title: Proverbs 15:30
text: ¶That which enlighteneth the eyes rejoiceth the heart; good tidings make the bones fat.

title: Proverbs 15:31
text: ¶The ear that heareth the reproof of life shall abide among the wise.

title: Proverbs 15:32
text: ¶He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul; but he that heareth reproof getteth sense.

title: Proverbs 15:33
text: ¶The fear of Jehovah is the discipline of wisdom, and before honour [goeth] humility.

title: Proverbs 16:1
text: ¶The purposes of the heart are of man, but the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 16:2
text: ¶All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but Jehovah weigheth the spirits.

title: Proverbs 16:3
text: ¶Commit thy works unto Jehovah, and thy thoughts shall be established.

title: Proverbs 16:4
text: ¶Jehovah hath wrought everything on his own account, yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.

title: Proverbs 16:5
text: ¶Every proud heart is an abomination to Jehovah: hand for hand, he shall not be held innocent.

title: Proverbs 16:6
text: ¶By loving-kindness and truth iniquity is atoned for; and by the fear of Jehovah [men] depart from evil.

title: Proverbs 16:7
text: ¶When a man's ways please Jehovah, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

title: Proverbs 16:8
text: ¶Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues without right.

title: Proverbs 16:9
text: ¶The heart of man deviseth his way, but Jehovah directeth his steps.

title: Proverbs 16:10
text: ¶An oracle is on the lips of the king: his mouth will not err in judgment.

title: Proverbs 16:11
text: ¶The just balance and scales are Jehovah's; all the weights of the bag are his work.

title: Proverbs 16:12
text: ¶It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness; for the throne is established by righteousness.

title: Proverbs 16:13
text: ¶Righteous lips are the delight of kings, and they love him that speaketh aright.

title: Proverbs 16:14
text: ¶The fury of a king is [as] messengers of death; but a wise man will pacify it.

title: Proverbs 16:15
text: In the light of the king's countenance is life, and his favour is as a cloud of the latter rain.

title: Proverbs 16:16
text: ¶How much better is it to get wisdom than fine gold, and the getting of intelligence to be preferred to silver!

title: Proverbs 16:17
text: ¶The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: he that taketh heed to his way keepeth his soul.

title: Proverbs 16:18
text: ¶Pride [goeth] before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

title: Proverbs 16:19
text: ¶Better is it to be of a humble spirit with the meek, than to divide the spoil with the proud.

title: Proverbs 16:20
text: ¶He that giveth heed to the word shall find good; and whoso confideth in Jehovah, happy is he.

title: Proverbs 16:21
text: ¶The wise in heart is called intelligent, and the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.

title: Proverbs 16:22
text: ¶Wisdom is a fountain of life for him that hath it; but the instruction of fools is folly.

title: Proverbs 16:23
text: ¶The heart of the wise maketh his mouth intelligent, and upon his lips increaseth learning.

title: Proverbs 16:24
text: ¶Pleasant words are [as] a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health for the bones.

title: Proverbs 16:25
text: ¶There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof is the ways of death.

title: Proverbs 16:26
text: ¶The appetite of the labourer laboureth for him, for his mouth urgeth him on.

title: Proverbs 16:27
text: ¶A man of Belial diggeth up evil, and on his lips there is as a scorching fire.

title: Proverbs 16:28
text: A false man soweth contention; and a talebearer separateth very friends.

title: Proverbs 16:29
text: ¶A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into a way that is not good.

title: Proverbs 16:30
text: He that shutteth his eyes, [it is] to devise froward things; biting his lips, he bringeth evil to pass.

title: Proverbs 16:31
text: ¶The hoary head is a crown of glory, [if] it is found in the way of righteousness.

title: Proverbs 16:32
text: ¶He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.

title: Proverbs 16:33
text: ¶The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole decision is of Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 17:1
text: ¶Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than a house full of feasting [with] strife.

title: Proverbs 17:2
text: ¶A wise servant shall rule over a son that causeth shame, and shall have part in the inheritance among the brethren.

title: Proverbs 17:3
text: ¶The fining-pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but Jehovah trieth the hearts.

title: Proverbs 17:4
text: ¶The evil-doer giveth heed to iniquitous lips; the liar giveth ear to a mischievous tongue.

title: Proverbs 17:5
text: ¶Whoso mocketh a poor [man] reproacheth his Maker; he that is glad at calamity shall not be held innocent.

title: Proverbs 17:6
text: ¶Children's children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.

title: Proverbs 17:7
text: ¶Excellent speech becometh not a vile [man]; how much less do lying lips a noble!

title: Proverbs 17:8
text: ¶A gift is a precious stone in the eyes of the possessor: whithersoever it turneth it prospereth.

title: Proverbs 17:9
text: ¶He that covereth transgression seeketh love; but he that bringeth a matter up again separateth very friends.

title: Proverbs 17:10
text: ¶A reproof entereth more deeply into him that hath understanding than a hundred stripes into a fool.

title: Proverbs 17:11
text: ¶An evil [man] seeketh only rebellion; but a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

title: Proverbs 17:12
text: ¶Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man rather than a fool in his folly.

title: Proverbs 17:13
text: ¶Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.

title: Proverbs 17:14
text: ¶The beginning of contention is [as] when one letteth out water; therefore leave off strife before it become vehement.

title: Proverbs 17:15
text: ¶He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the righteous, even they both are abomination to Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 17:16
text: ¶To what purpose is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing [he] hath no sense?

title: Proverbs 17:17
text: ¶The friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

title: Proverbs 17:18
text: ¶A senseless man striketh hands, becoming surety for his neighbour.

title: Proverbs 17:19
text: ¶He loveth transgression that loveth a quarrel; he that maketh high his gate seeketh destruction.

title: Proverbs 17:20
text: ¶He that hath a perverse heart findeth no good; and he that shifteth about with his tongue falleth into evil.

title: Proverbs 17:21
text: ¶He that begetteth a fool [doeth it] to his sorrow, and the father of a vile [man] hath no joy.

title: Proverbs 17:22
text: ¶A joyful heart promoteth healing; but a broken spirit drieth up the bones.

title: Proverbs 17:23
text: ¶A wicked [man] taketh a gift out of the bosom, to pervert the paths of judgment.

title: Proverbs 17:24
text: ¶Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.

title: Proverbs 17:25
text: ¶A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bore him.

title: Proverbs 17:26
text: ¶To punish a righteous [man] is not good, nor to strike nobles because of [their] uprightness.

title: Proverbs 17:27
text: ¶He that hath knowledge spareth his words; and a man of understanding is of a cool spirit.

title: Proverbs 17:28
text: Even a fool when he holdeth his peace is reckoned wise, [and] he that shutteth his lips, intelligent.

title: Proverbs 18:1
text: ¶He that separateth himself seeketh [his] pleasure, he is vehement against all sound wisdom.

title: Proverbs 18:2
text: ¶A fool hath no delight in understanding, but only that his heart may reveal itself.

title: Proverbs 18:3
text: ¶When the wicked cometh, there cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach.

title: Proverbs 18:4
text: ¶The words of a man's mouth are deep waters, [and] the fountain of wisdom is a gushing brook.

title: Proverbs 18:5
text: ¶It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to wrong the righteous in judgment.

title: Proverbs 18:6
text: ¶A fool's lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for stripes.

title: Proverbs 18:7
text: A fool's mouth is destruction to him, and his lips are a snare to his soul.

title: Proverbs 18:8
text: ¶The words of a talebearer are as dainty morsels, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 18:9
text: ¶He also who is indolent in his work is brother of the destroyer.

title: Proverbs 18:10
text: ¶The name of Jehovah is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.

title: Proverbs 18:11
text: ¶The rich man's wealth is his strong city, and as a high wall in his own imagination.

title: Proverbs 18:12
text: ¶Before destruction the heart of man is haughty; and before honour [goeth] humility.

title: Proverbs 18:13
text: ¶He that giveth answer before he heareth, it is folly and shame unto him.

title: Proverbs 18:14
text: ¶The spirit of a man sustaineth his infirmity; but a broken spirit who can bear?

title: Proverbs 18:15
text: ¶The heart of an intelligent [man] getteth knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.

title: Proverbs 18:16
text: ¶A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.

title: Proverbs 18:17
text: ¶He that is first in his own cause [seemeth] just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.

title: Proverbs 18:18
text: ¶The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty.

title: Proverbs 18:19
text: ¶A brother offended is [harder to be won] than a strong city; and contentions are as the bars of a palace.

title: Proverbs 18:20
text: ¶A man's belly is satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; with the increase of his lips is he satisfied.

title: Proverbs 18:21
text: ¶Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

title: Proverbs 18:22
text: ¶Whoso hath found a wife hath found a good thing, and hath obtained favour from Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 18:23
text: ¶He that is poor speaketh with supplications, but the rich answereth roughly.

title: Proverbs 18:24
text: ¶A man of [many] friends will come to ruin but there is a friend [that] sticketh closer than a brother.

title: Proverbs 19:1
text: ¶Better is a poor [man] that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.

title: Proverbs 19:2
text: ¶Also that a person be without knowledge is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet maketh false steps.

title: Proverbs 19:3
text: ¶The folly of man distorteth his way, and his heart is irritated against Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 19:4
text: ¶Wealth addeth many friends; but the poor is separated from his friend.

title: Proverbs 19:5
text: ¶A false witness shall not be held innocent, and he that uttereth lies shall not escape.

title: Proverbs 19:6
text: ¶Many court the favour of a noble; and every one is friend to a man that giveth.

title: Proverbs 19:7
text: All the brethren of a poor [man] hate him; how much more do his friends go far from him: he pursueth [them] with words, --they are not [to be found].

title: Proverbs 19:8
text: ¶He that getteth sense loveth his own soul; he that keepeth understanding shall find good.

title: Proverbs 19:9
text: ¶A false witness shall not be held innocent, and he that uttereth lies shall perish.

title: Proverbs 19:10
text: ¶Good living beseemeth not a fool; how much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

title: Proverbs 19:11
text: ¶The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger, and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.

title: Proverbs 19:12
text: ¶The king's displeasure is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour is as dew upon the grass.

title: Proverbs 19:13
text: ¶A foolish son is the calamity of his father; and the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.

title: Proverbs 19:14
text: ¶House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers; but a prudent wife is from Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 19:15
text: ¶Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep, and the idle soul shall suffer hunger.

title: Proverbs 19:16
text: ¶He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; he that is careless of his ways shall die.

title: Proverbs 19:17
text: ¶He that is gracious to the poor lendeth unto Jehovah; and what he hath bestowed will he repay unto him.

title: Proverbs 19:18
text: ¶Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; but set not thy soul upon killing him.

title: Proverbs 19:19
text: ¶A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment; for if thou deliver [him], yet thou must do it again.

title: Proverbs 19:20
text: ¶Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.

title: Proverbs 19:21
text: ¶Many are the thoughts in a man's heart, but the counsel of Jehovah, that doth stand.

title: Proverbs 19:22
text: ¶The charm of a man is his kindness; and a poor [man] is better than a liar.

title: Proverbs 19:23
text: ¶The fear of Jehovah [tendeth] to life, and he [that hath it] shall rest satisfied without being visited with evil.

title: Proverbs 19:24
text: ¶A sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, and will not even bring it to his mouth again.

title: Proverbs 19:25
text: ¶Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware; reprove the intelligent, and he will understand knowledge.

title: Proverbs 19:26
text: ¶He that ruineth [his] father and chaseth away [his] mother is a son that causeth shame and bringeth reproach.

title: Proverbs 19:27
text: ¶Cease, my son, to hear the instruction which causeth to stray from the words of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 19:28
text: ¶A witness of Belial scorneth judgment, and the mouth of the wicked swalloweth down iniquity.

title: Proverbs 19:29
text: ¶Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of the foolish.

title: Proverbs 20:1
text: ¶Wine is a scorner, strong drink is raging; and whoso erreth thereby is not wise.

title: Proverbs 20:2
text: ¶The terror of a king is as the roaring of a lion: he that provoketh him to anger sinneth against his own soul.

title: Proverbs 20:3
text: ¶It is an honour for a man to cease from strife; but every fool rusheth into it.

title: Proverbs 20:4
text: ¶The sluggard will not plough by reason of the winter; he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.

title: Proverbs 20:5
text: ¶Counsel in the heart of man is deep water, and a man of understanding draweth it out.

title: Proverbs 20:6
text: ¶Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; but a faithful man who shall find?

title: Proverbs 20:7
text: ¶The righteous walketh in his integrity: blessed are his children after him!

title: Proverbs 20:8
text: ¶A king sitting on the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.

title: Proverbs 20:9
text: ¶Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?

title: Proverbs 20:10
text: ¶Divers weights, divers measures, even both of them are abomination to Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 20:11
text: ¶Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.

title: Proverbs 20:12
text: ¶The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.

title: Proverbs 20:13
text: ¶Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, [and] thou shalt be satisfied with bread.

title: Proverbs 20:14
text: ¶Bad! bad! saith the buyer; but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.

title: Proverbs 20:15
text: ¶There is gold, and a multitude of rubies; but the lips of knowledge are a precious Jewel.

title: Proverbs 20:16
text: ¶Take his garment that is become surety [for] another, and hold him in pledge for strangers.

title: Proverbs 20:17
text: ¶Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

title: Proverbs 20:18
text: ¶Plans are established by counsel; and with good advice make war.

title: Proverbs 20:19
text: ¶He that goeth about talebearing revealeth secrets; therefore meddle not with him that openeth his lips.

title: Proverbs 20:20
text: ¶Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in the blackest darkness.

title: Proverbs 20:21
text: ¶An inheritance obtained hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.

title: Proverbs 20:22
text: ¶Say not, I will recompense evil: wait on Jehovah, and he shall save thee.

title: Proverbs 20:23
text: ¶Divers weights are an abomination unto Jehovah; and a false balance is not good.

title: Proverbs 20:24
text: ¶The steps of a man are from Jehovah; and how can a man understand his own way?

title: Proverbs 20:25
text: ¶It is a snare to a man rashly to say, It is hallowed, and after vows to make inquiry.

title: Proverbs 20:26
text: ¶A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.

title: Proverbs 20:27
text: ¶Man's spirit is the lamp of Jehovah, searching all the inner parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 20:28
text: ¶Mercy and truth preserve the king; and he upholdeth his throne by mercy.

title: Proverbs 20:29
text: ¶The glory of young men is their strength; and the beauty of old men is the grey head.

title: Proverbs 20:30
text: ¶Wounding stripes purge away evil, and strokes [purge] the inner parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 21:1
text: ¶The king's heart in the hand of Jehovah is [as] brooks of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

title: Proverbs 21:2
text: ¶Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; but Jehovah weigheth the hearts.

title: Proverbs 21:3
text: ¶To exercise justice and judgment is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.

title: Proverbs 21:4
text: ¶Lofty eyes, and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, is sin.

title: Proverbs 21:5
text: ¶The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty, only to want.

title: Proverbs 21:6
text: ¶The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting breath of them that seek death.

title: Proverbs 21:7
text: ¶The devastation of the wicked sweepeth them away, because they refuse to do what is right.

title: Proverbs 21:8
text: ¶Very crooked is the way of a guilty man; but as for the pure, his work is upright.

title: Proverbs 21:9
text: ¶It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a contentious woman, and a house in common.

title: Proverbs 21:10
text: ¶The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.

title: Proverbs 21:11
text: ¶When the scorner is punished, the simple becometh wise; and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.

title: Proverbs 21:12
text: ¶One that is righteous wisely considereth the house of the wicked: he overthroweth the wicked to [their] ruin.

title: Proverbs 21:13
text: ¶Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also himself shall cry, and shall not be heard.

title: Proverbs 21:14
text: ¶A gift in secret pacifieth anger; and a present in the bosom, vehement fury.

title: Proverbs 21:15
text: ¶It is joy to a righteous [man] to do what is right; but it is ruin for the workers of iniquity.

title: Proverbs 21:16
text: ¶The man that wandereth out of the way of wisdom shall abide in the congregation of the dead.

title: Proverbs 21:17
text: ¶He that loveth mirth shall be a poor man; he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.

title: Proverbs 21:18
text: ¶The wicked is a ransom for the righteous, and a treacherous [man] in the stead of the upright.

title: Proverbs 21:19
text: ¶It is better to dwell in a desert land. than with a contentious and irritable woman.

title: Proverbs 21:20
text: ¶There is costly store and oil in the dwelling of a wise [man]; but a foolish man swalloweth it up.

title: Proverbs 21:21
text: ¶He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.

title: Proverbs 21:22
text: ¶A wise [man] scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.

title: Proverbs 21:23
text: ¶Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.

title: Proverbs 21:24
text: ¶Proud, arrogant, scorner is his name who dealeth in proud wrath.

title: Proverbs 21:25
text: ¶The desire of the sluggard killeth him; for his hands refuse to work:

title: Proverbs 21:26
text: He coveteth greedily all the day long; but the righteous giveth and spareth not.

title: Proverbs 21:27
text: ¶The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more when they bring it with a wicked purpose!

title: Proverbs 21:28
text: ¶A lying witness shall perish; and a man that heareth shall speak constantly.

title: Proverbs 21:29
text: ¶A wicked man hardeneth his face; but as for the upright, he establisheth his way.

title: Proverbs 21:30
text: ¶There is no wisdom, nor understanding, nor counsel against Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 21:31
text: The horse is prepared for the day of battle; but safety is of Jehovah.

title: Proverbs 22:1
text: ¶A [good] name is rather to be chosen than great riches; loving favour rather than silver and gold.

title: Proverbs 22:2
text: ¶The rich and poor meet together; Jehovah is the maker of them all.

title: Proverbs 22:3
text: ¶A prudent [man] seeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.

title: Proverbs 22:4
text: ¶The reward of humility [and] the fear of Jehovah is riches, and honour, and life.

title: Proverbs 22:5
text: ¶Thorns [and] snares are in the way of the perverse: he that keepeth his soul holdeth himself far from them.

title: Proverbs 22:6
text: ¶Train up the child according to the tenor of his way, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

title: Proverbs 22:7
text: ¶The rich ruleth over the poor; and the borrower is servant to the lender.

title: Proverbs 22:8
text: ¶He that soweth unrighteousness shall reap iniquity, and the rod of his wrath shall have an end.

title: Proverbs 22:9
text: ¶He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed, for he giveth of his bread to the poor.

title: Proverbs 22:10
text: ¶Cast out the scorner, and contention will depart, and strife and ignominy shall cease.

title: Proverbs 22:11
text: ¶He that loveth pureness of heart, upon whose lips is grace, the king is his friend.

title: Proverbs 22:12
text: ¶The eyes of Jehovah preserve knowledge; but he overthroweth the words of the unfaithful.

title: Proverbs 22:13
text: ¶The sluggard saith, There is a lion without, I shall be killed in the streets!

title: Proverbs 22:14
text: ¶The mouth of strange women is a deep ditch: he with whom Jehovah is displeased shall fall therein.

title: Proverbs 22:15
text: ¶Folly is bound in the heart of a child; the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

title: Proverbs 22:16
text: ¶He that oppresseth the poor, it is to enrich him; he that giveth to the rich, [bringeth] only to want.

title: Proverbs 22:17
text: ¶Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thy heart unto my knowledge.

title: Proverbs 22:18
text: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee: they shall be together fitted on thy lips.

title: Proverbs 22:19
text: That thy confidence may be in Jehovah, I have made [them] known to thee this day, even to thee.

title: Proverbs 22:20
text: Have not I written to thee excellent things, in counsels and knowledge,

title: Proverbs 22:21
text: that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?

title: Proverbs 22:22
text: ¶Rob not the poor, because he is poor, neither oppress the afflicted in the gate;

title: Proverbs 22:23
text: for Jehovah will plead their cause, and despoil the soul of those that despoil them.

title: Proverbs 22:24
text: ¶Make no friendship with an angry man, and go not with a furious man;

title: Proverbs 22:25
text: lest thou learn his paths, and get a snare to thy soul.

title: Proverbs 22:26
text: ¶Be not of them that strike hands, of them that are sureties for debts:

title: Proverbs 22:27
text: if thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?

title: Proverbs 22:28
text: ¶Remove not the ancient landmark which thy fathers have set.

title: Proverbs 22:29
text: ¶Hast thou seen a man diligent in his work? He shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before the mean.

title: Proverbs 23:1
text: ¶When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider well who is before thee;

title: Proverbs 23:2
text: and put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.

title: Proverbs 23:3
text: Be not desirous of his dainties; for they are deceitful food.

title: Proverbs 23:4
text: ¶Weary not thyself to become rich; cease from thine own intelligence:

title: Proverbs 23:5
text: wilt thou set thine eyes upon it, it is gone; for indeed it maketh itself wings and it flieth away as an eagle towards the heavens.

title: Proverbs 23:6
text: ¶Eat thou not the food of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainties.

title: Proverbs 23:7
text: For as he thinketh in his soul, so is he. Eat and drink! will he say unto thee; but his heart is not with thee.

title: Proverbs 23:8
text: Thy morsel which thou hast eaten must thou vomit up, and thou wilt have wasted thy sweet words.

title: Proverbs 23:9
text: ¶Speak not in the ears of a foolish [man], for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.

title: Proverbs 23:10
text: ¶Remove not the ancient landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:

title: Proverbs 23:11
text: for their redeemer is mighty; he will plead their cause against thee.

title: Proverbs 23:12
text: ¶Apply thy heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.

title: Proverbs 23:13
text: Withhold not correction from the child; for [if] thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die:

title: Proverbs 23:14
text: thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.

title: Proverbs 23:15
text: My son, if thy heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine;

title: Proverbs 23:16
text: and my reins shall exult, when thy lips speak right things.

title: Proverbs 23:17
text: ¶Let not thy heart envy sinners, but [be thou] in the fear of Jehovah all the day;

title: Proverbs 23:18
text: for surely there is a result, and thine expectation shall not be cut off.

title: Proverbs 23:19
text: ¶Thou, my son, hear and be wise, and direct thy heart in the way.

title: Proverbs 23:20
text: Be not among winebibbers, among riotous eaters of flesh.

title: Proverbs 23:21
text: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; and drowsiness clotheth with rags.

title: Proverbs 23:22
text: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.

title: Proverbs 23:23
text: Buy the truth, and sell it not; wisdom, and instruction, and intelligence.

title: Proverbs 23:24
text: The father of a righteous [man] shall greatly rejoice, and he that begetteth a wise [son] shall have joy of him:

title: Proverbs 23:25
text: let thy father and thy mother have joy, and let her that bore thee rejoice.

title: Proverbs 23:26
text: My son, give me thy heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

title: Proverbs 23:27
text: For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.

title: Proverbs 23:28
text: She also lieth in wait as a robber, and increaseth the treacherous among men.

title: Proverbs 23:29
text: ¶Who hath woe? Who hath sorrow? Who contentions? Who complaining? Who wounds without cause? Who redness of eyes?

title: Proverbs 23:30
text: --They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to try mixed wine.

title: Proverbs 23:31
text: Look not upon the wine when it is red, when it sparkleth in the cup, and goeth down smoothly:

title: Proverbs 23:32
text: at the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.

title: Proverbs 23:33
text: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thy heart shall speak froward things;

title: Proverbs 23:34
text: and thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, and as he that lieth down upon the top of a mast:

title: Proverbs 23:35
text: --''They have smitten me, [and] I am not sore; they have beaten me, [and] I knew it not. When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.''

title: Proverbs 24:1
text: ¶Be not thou envious of evil men, neither desire to be with them;

title: Proverbs 24:2
text: for their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.

title: Proverbs 24:3
text: ¶Through wisdom is a house built, and by understanding it is established;

title: Proverbs 24:4
text: and by knowledge are the chambers filled with all precious and pleasant substance.

title: Proverbs 24:5
text: A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge increaseth strength.

title: Proverbs 24:6
text: For with good advice shalt thou make thy war; and in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

title: Proverbs 24:7
text: ¶Wisdom is too high for a fool: he will not open his mouth in the gate.

title: Proverbs 24:8
text: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a master of intrigues.

title: Proverbs 24:9
text: The purpose of folly is sin, and the scorner is an abomination to men.

title: Proverbs 24:10
text: ¶[If] thou losest courage in the day of trouble, thy strength is small.

title: Proverbs 24:11
text: ¶Deliver them that are taken forth unto death, and withdraw not from them that stagger to slaughter.

title: Proverbs 24:12
text: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not, will not he that weigheth the hearts consider it? And he that preserveth thy soul, he knoweth it; and he rendereth to man according to his work.

title: Proverbs 24:13
text: ¶Eat honey, my son, for it is good; and a honeycomb is sweet to thy taste:

title: Proverbs 24:14
text: so consider wisdom for thy soul; if thou hast found it, there shall be a result, and thine expectation shall not be cut off.

title: Proverbs 24:15
text: ¶Lay not wait, O wicked [man], against the dwelling of the righteous; lay not waste his resting-place.

title: Proverbs 24:16
text: For the righteous falleth seven times, and riseth up again; but the wicked stumble into disaster.

title: Proverbs 24:17
text: ¶Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thy heart be glad when he stumbleth;

title: Proverbs 24:18
text: lest Jehovah see it, and it be evil in his sight, and he turn away his anger from him.

title: Proverbs 24:19
text: ¶Fret not thyself because of evil-doers, [and] be not envious of the wicked:

title: Proverbs 24:20
text: for there shall be no future to the evil [man]; the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

title: Proverbs 24:21
text: ¶My son, fear Jehovah and the king: meddle not with them that are given to change.

title: Proverbs 24:22
text: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?

title: Proverbs 24:23
text: ¶These things also come from the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.

title: Proverbs 24:24
text: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous, peoples shall curse him, nations shall abhor him;

title: Proverbs 24:25
text: but to them that rebuke [him] shall be delight, and a good blessing cometh upon them.

title: Proverbs 24:26
text: He kisseth the lips who giveth a right answer.

title: Proverbs 24:27
text: ¶Prepare thy work without, and put thy field in order, and afterwards build thy house.

title: Proverbs 24:28
text: ¶Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and wouldest thou deceive with thy lips?

title: Proverbs 24:29
text: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me, I will render to the man according to his work.

title: Proverbs 24:30
text: ¶I went by the field of a sluggard, and by the vineyard of a man void of understanding;

title: Proverbs 24:31
text: and lo, it was all grown over with thistles, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and its stone wall was broken down.

title: Proverbs 24:32
text: Then I looked, I took it to heart; I saw, I received instruction:

title: Proverbs 24:33
text: --A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest!

title: Proverbs 24:34
text: So shall thy poverty come [as] a roving plunderer, and thy penury as an armed man.

title: Proverbs 25:1
text: ¶These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah transcribed.

title: Proverbs 25:2
text: ¶It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; but the glory of kings is to search out a thing.

title: Proverbs 25:3
text: The heavens for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.

title: Proverbs 25:4
text: ¶Take away the dross from the silver, and there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner:

title: Proverbs 25:5
text: take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.

title: Proverbs 25:6
text: ¶Put not thyself forward in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of the great;

title: Proverbs 25:7
text: for better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes see.

title: Proverbs 25:8
text: ¶Go not forth hastily to strive, lest [thou know not] what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.

title: Proverbs 25:9
text: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour, but reveal not the secret of another;

title: Proverbs 25:10
text: lest he that heareth [it] disgrace thee, and thine evil report turn not away.

title: Proverbs 25:11
text: ¶[As] apples of gold in pictures of silver, is a word spoken in season.

title: Proverbs 25:12
text: An ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, is a wise reprover upon an attentive ear.

title: Proverbs 25:13
text: ¶As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, [so] is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.

title: Proverbs 25:14
text: ¶Clouds and wind without rain, [so] is a man that boasteth himself of a false gift.

title: Proverbs 25:15
text: ¶By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

title: Proverbs 25:16
text: ¶Hast thou found honey? Eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be surfeited therewith, and vomit it.

title: Proverbs 25:17
text: ¶Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee and hate thee.

title: Proverbs 25:18
text: ¶A maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow, is a man that beareth false witness against his neighbour.

title: Proverbs 25:19
text: ¶A broken tooth, and a tottering foot, is confidence in an unfaithful [man] in the day of trouble.

title: Proverbs 25:20
text: ¶[As] he that taketh off a garment in cold weather, [and as] vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to a sad heart.

title: Proverbs 25:21
text: ¶If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

title: Proverbs 25:22
text: for thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and Jehovah shall reward thee.

title: Proverbs 25:23
text: ¶The north wind bringeth forth rain, and the angry countenance a backbiting tongue.

title: Proverbs 25:24
text: ¶It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a contentious woman, and a house in common.

title: Proverbs 25:25
text: ¶[As] cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.

title: Proverbs 25:26
text: ¶A troubled fountain, and a defiled well, is a righteous [man] that giveth way before the wicked.

title: Proverbs 25:27
text: ¶It is not good to eat much honey; and to search into weighty matters is [itself] a weight.

title: Proverbs 25:28
text: ¶He that hath no rule over his own spirit is [as] a city broken down, without walls.

title: Proverbs 26:1
text: ¶As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour beseemeth not a fool.

title: Proverbs 26:2
text: ¶As the sparrow for flitting about, as the swallow for flying, so a curse undeserved shall not come.

title: Proverbs 26:3
text: ¶A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the back of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:4
text: ¶Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.

title: Proverbs 26:5
text: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.

title: Proverbs 26:6
text: ¶He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off [his own] feet, [and] drinketh damage.

title: Proverbs 26:7
text: The legs of the lame hang loose; so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:8
text: As a bag of gems in a stoneheap, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.

title: Proverbs 26:9
text: [As] a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

title: Proverbs 26:10
text: ¶A master roughly worketh every one: he both hireth the fool and hireth passers-by.

title: Proverbs 26:11
text: ¶As a dog turneth back to its vomit, [so] a fool repeateth his folly.

title: Proverbs 26:12
text: ¶Hast thou seen a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope of a fool than of him.

title: Proverbs 26:13
text: ¶The sluggard saith, There is a fierce lion in the way; a lion is in the midst of the streets!

title: Proverbs 26:14
text: ¶[As] the door turneth upon its hinges, so the sluggard upon his bed.

title: Proverbs 26:15
text: ¶The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish: it wearieth him to bring it again to his mouth.

title: Proverbs 26:16
text: ¶A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven [men] that answer discreetly.

title: Proverbs 26:17
text: ¶He that passing by vexeth himself with strife belonging not to him, is [like] one that taketh a dog by the ears.

title: Proverbs 26:18
text: ¶As a madman who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,

title: Proverbs 26:19
text: so is a man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am I not in sport?

title: Proverbs 26:20
text: ¶Where no wood is, the fire goeth out; and where there is no talebearer, the contention ceaseth.

title: Proverbs 26:21
text: [As] coals for hot coals, and wood for fire, so is a contentious man to inflame strife.

title: Proverbs 26:22
text: The words of a talebearer are as dainty morsels, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

title: Proverbs 26:23
text: ¶Ardent lips, and a wicked heart, are [as] an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.

title: Proverbs 26:24
text: ¶He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, but he layeth up deceit within him:

title: Proverbs 26:25
text: when his voice is gracious, believe him not, for there are seven abominations in his heart.

title: Proverbs 26:26
text: Though [his] hatred is covered by dissimulation, his wickedness shall be made manifest in the congregation.

title: Proverbs 26:27
text: ¶Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein; and he that rolleth a stone, it shall return upon him.

title: Proverbs 26:28
text: ¶A lying tongue hateth those that are injured by it, and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.

title: Proverbs 27:1
text: ¶Boast not thyself of to-morrow, for thou knowest not what a day will bring forth.

title: Proverbs 27:2
text: ¶Let another praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

title: Proverbs 27:3
text: ¶A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's vexation is heavier than them both.

title: Proverbs 27:4
text: Fury is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before jealousy?

title: Proverbs 27:5
text: ¶Open rebuke is better than hidden love.

title: Proverbs 27:6
text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

title: Proverbs 27:7
text: ¶The full soul trampleth on a honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

title: Proverbs 27:8
text: ¶As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.

title: Proverbs 27:9
text: ¶Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart; and the sweetness of one's friend is [the fruit] of hearty counsel.

title: Proverbs 27:10
